newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen leader forms new govt, national guard.
newsitem.headline: Chechen leader forms new govt, national guard.

text.p: Chechnya's President Aslan Maskhadov on Wednesday unveiled a new government and ordered creation of a national guard, Russian news agencies said.

Maskhadov, who swept to power in the breakaway region's first post-war election in January, kept Interior Minister Kazbek Makhashev and the head of the state oil company Khozhakhmed Yarikhanov in their respective posts.

But in a gesture towards the popular runner-up for the presidency, Maskhadov also brought several allies of guerrilla leader Shamil Basayev into the government, Interfax news agency said. It added that their new positions were still unclear.

Interfax named Isa Astamirov, who it said had previously held no high official posts, as economy minister and Akhmed Zakayev, a leading local actor turned successful guerrilla leader, as culture minister.
Itar-Tass news agency said Maskhadov had signed a decree setting up a new national guard from the ranks of the "most active participants in the war" against Russia.
It quoted the document as saying Chechnya needed the expertise and commitment of such people during the difficult post-war period of reconstruction.

Bringing large numbers of young fighters back into civilian life is a major social problem in Chechnya, which is still awash with weapons and ammunition and where the separatist authorities are struggling to restore the rule of law.

Tass said it was not immediately clear what form the new guard would take but added that it might present a rival force to the current presidential guard, reported to be closer to former acting president Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev than to Maskhadov.
Earlier this week, in a possible sign of tension between Chechnya's leaders, a bomb exploded in the capital Grozny just after a convoy carrying Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov passed the spot.

Nobody was hurt in the blast but Interfax said Interior Ministry officials had not ruled out a possible assassination attempt against Udugov, the rebels' propaganda chief during the war and who also ran for the presidency in January.
Chechnya is currently locked in negotiations with Russia aimed at mapping out a new economic relationship.
